newsitem.title: USA: DOT prohibits Millon from leasing.
newsitem.headline: DOT prohibits Millon from leasing.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Transportation has prohibited grounded Millon Air from wet-leasing aircraft, as it had been doing since an accident in October, a DOT spokesman said Thursday.
"We gave them a one-month exemption (to wet-lease) and that one month expired," DOT spokesman Bill Mosley said.

The all-cargo Millon had been trying to continue to serve its customers by wet-leasing aircraft since it voluntarily grounded itself in October as requested by the Federal Aviation Administration. The grounding followed an accident in Manta, Ecuador.
Although it was not allowed to operate its own planes, privately-held Million was allowed to lease aircraft from others as long as it did not provide crew or maintenance.

But on Dec. 6, DOT wrote Million that "it has determined that the carrier has effectively ceased air carrier operations" and "that it may not resume operations, including operations conducted under wet leases until such time as the Department has redetermined that it is fit to do so."
Millon officials did not return phone calls for comment.
In the October accident, Millon's 29-year-old Boeing 707 crashed into a residential neighborhood in Manta, Ecuador killing at least 25 people and injuring at least 60 more.
The FAA is still reviewing Millon's operations and the DOT must complete its fitness review before Millon can resume flying. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
